title: Lesson 32 - Archiving and purging scenarios: what to archive, when, compliance
description: Given a customer scenario, recommend an archiving and purging plan that is optimal for the customer's data storage management needs, deciding what to archive, when, and how to satisfy compliance requirements.

questions.question: A customer must purge customer data to satisfy GDPR storage limitation but also retain financial transactions for 7 years. What is the best plan?
options: Delete all data older than one year
Anonymize personal fields on transactions older than the retention point while retaining the financial records for 7 years
Archive everything to a Big Object with no deletion
questions.explanation: Anonymize-and-retain satisfies erasure of personal data while preserving required financial records; indiscriminate deletion (A) breaks retention rules, and B/D violate storage limitation.

questions.question: Which TWO should be part of an archiving/purging plan for a parent object with millions of child records?
options: Handle referential integrity by archiving children or rerouting lookups
Delete the parent and leave dangling child lookups
Define retention per data category with any legal hold
Disable audit logging to speed the job
questions.explanation: Referential-integrity handling (A) and per-category retention with legal hold (C) are essential; dangling lookups (B) corrupt data and disabling audit logging (D) removes the evidence.

questions.question: Why choose an off-platform archive store over an on-platform Big Object for some data categories?
options: It keeps data editable in Salesforce
It frees Salesforce storage when the platform does not need to serve the data
It avoids the need for retention rules
questions.explanation: Off-platform archiving frees Salesforce storage when native query is not required; it is not directly editable (A), does not add native reports (C), and never removes retention obligations (D).
